basics.name: Smayan A. Khanna
basics.label: MS Computer Science Student (UChicago)
basics.summary: MS Computer Science student focused on AI for Science, especially representation learning and coarse-graining for physical and biological systems using geometric deep learning and graph neural networks.

work.name: University of Chicago - James Franck Institute, Vitelli Group
work.summary: Researching deep-learning techniques for representation learning in biological and physical systems; developed contrastive GNN-based methods and led a first-author project on scaling behavior of graph contrastive learning.
highlights: Developed a contrastive algorithm combining GNNs with statistical-physics ideas to coarse-grain inhomogeneous graph data
Led first-author study on effectiveness and scaling behavior of Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) for unsupervised graph classification

work.name: Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL), AlphaGen
work.position: Data Science Intern - Stock Prediction Model Development
work.summary: Built ML pipelines for short-term stock prediction, feature selection, and backtesting.
highlights: Implemented PCA + RFE pipeline for dimensionality reduction and feature selection
Built backtesting framework (~60% prediction accuracy) and explored hyperparameter optimization (Random + Bayesian search)

work.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Dunkel Group (with the Flavell Lab)
work.summary: Studied the brain–behavior link in C. elegans; built Julia tooling for analysis/visualization and applied PCA, graph theory, and compressed sensing.
highlights: Developed a Julia pipeline for analysis and visualization of neural trace activity datasets
Used Matching Pursuit to identify a superior basis for time-series reconstruction, improving accuracy by ~20% vs random bases

work.name: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, Ferguson Lab (University of Chicago)
work.summary: Co-developed generative backmapping models for proteins/DNA using Conditional Flow Matching and EGNNs; optimized inference and evaluated ODE solvers.
highlights: Trained and fine-tuned generative models on DNA–protein structures
Optimized inference by evaluating ODE solvers; achieved >99% reconstruction accuracy

work.name: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, Tokmakoff Group & Prof. Andrew Ferguson (University of Chicago)
work.summary: Generated all-atom MD simulations of DNA for T-jump spectroscopy studies; automated topology creation and cluster workflows.
highlights: Streamlined nucleotide topologies, replica-exchange simulations, and cluster jobs via automation scripts

work.name: The Science Biome
work.summary: Created science communication videos on physics, math, and cosmology.
highlights: Grew channel to 2K subscribers and 90K+ views
Recognized by Prof. Steven Strogatz for a differential-equations video project
Featured/interviewed by Mumbai Mirror and The Times of India
